Subject: APAC edge onramp request — SparkNova latency-sensitive tier

Hi Alina / Peter,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our conversation, SparkNova is planning a latency-sensitive inference tier for Q4 that needs a nearby APAC footprint (Singapore) for sub-40ms tail latency to end-users in SEA. The deal is moving quickly on your side and procurement asked us for a concrete capacity plan so they can map costs into the SOW.

Attached is your forecast spreadsheet with the hourly TPS and expected token rates (sparknova_forecast_q4.csv). High-level ask from your product team:
- Sustained inference baseline: ~120 TPS (95th pct)
- Peak burst: 420 TPS for 2–3 minute spikes during batch events
- Seq lengths: 32–128 tokens typical; occasional 512 token evaluation jobs

For Redwood to support that with predictable SLAs, we think the right path is a small dedicated APAC pool (customer-dedicated nodes) with a micro-burst reserve for spikes. Please confirm the following so we can size the pool and lock in the Tranche/commit:
1) Target SLA/PU target (99th/95th latency expectations) and whether you need a hard SLO for tail latency.
2) Any procurement constraints on committed GPUs or monthly spend band.
3) Tentative timeline for signature (Procurement/Legal milestones).

If helpful, I can kick off an internal sizing thread and loop in Hannah for the node-level proposal. Proposed next steps: we produce a 2-week mutual action plan (MAP) that includes a canary window + production onramp.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0192

Alina — good notes. Quick answers:
- The 120 TPS number in the attached forecast is global; Singapore baseline should be treated as ~85 TPS. We'll dimension for regional baseline + a 3x burst multiplier.
- Burst cadence: our Dedicated product supports automatic burst lanes from a regional standby pool within ~90s for small bursts; for longer sustained bursts we recommend pre-provisioned burst nodes (warm) to avoid cold-start kernel warmups.
- Placeholder pricing: for a small dedicated micro-pool in SG (2x production nodes, 1x warm standby with autoscale) we estimate ~USD 28–36k/month depending on node type and commit term. I'll have Hannah add a technical cost estimate.

I've attached an initial SOW draft (RN_SOW_sparknova_v0.1.docx) and propose the following MAP:
Week 1: finalize capacity profile & legal terms
Week 2: provisioning + canary (1 week)
Week 3: production cutover and performance validation

If that timeline works, Hannah can propose node sizing and autoscale knobs to meet your tail latency targets.

Jordan

Attachment: RN_SOW_sparknova_v0.1.docx (docx, 120KB)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 13:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: APAC edge onramp request — SparkNova latency-sensitive tier

Looping in the technical sizing notes here. Based on the provided TPS and token profile, my recommendation for a low-latency Singapore micro-pool: 
- Production nodes: 2x nodes sized as 8xA10G-equivalent GPUs (or 4x A100-40GB equivalents) holding model shard + KV cache; this supports your 85 TPS baseline with headroom.
- Warm standby/burst: 1x node (same SKU) kept warm with prewarmed KV cache to handle 3x burst multiplier for up to 15 minutes.
- Autoscale: we set immediate short-window autoscale for 200ms + backoff for sustained load; also enable prefix caching for repeated inference paths.
- Quantization: use INT8 where acceptable for rate-limited workloads to reduce memory footprint and allow denser packing.

Preliminary cost estimate (ballpark): USD 32,500 / month for the configuration above with a 12-month commit. One-time onboarding SOW ~USD 12k. Exact numbers depend on choice of GPU family and regional infra premiums.

I've attached a quick workbook with CPU/GPU sizing and token-level assumptions (pool_proposal_singapore.xlsx). Karthik — can you confirm whether the deal-level triggers allow a 6-month ramp clause? That will affect commit tiering.

Thanks,
